prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts the camera wearer facing directly into a dense bush, with the wearer's torso and upper arms at the bottom edge (0.1 to 0.3 m away), extended hands and pruning loppers reaching 0.4 to 0.7 m forward into the foliage, overhanging leaves at the upper-left 0.3 to 0.6 m above and in front, and deeper interior branches receding to 1.5 to 3.0 m in the dark background. In frame 1, both hands hold the loppers low in front (about 0.2 m apart and 0.4 m from the camera), whereas across frames 2 to 5 the right arm reaches forward and upward to about 0.7 m to grasp a thin foreground vine within arm's reach while the left hand and loppers drop mostly out of view at the bottom-left and the grasped vine shifts closer to the camera in frames 3 and 4. Unlike the cluttered green-on-green RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the bright foreground vine, overhanging upper-left leaves, and reaching right arm from the recessed interior cavity of the bush, and shows the arm passing behind the foreground vine in frames 3 and 4. However, the map is unreliable along the thin lopper blades in frames 2 to 5, which blend into the background depth, and in the relative brightness of the right forearm, which appears artificially darker (farther) in frames 3 and 4 than in frames 2 and 5 despite maintaining a similar distance, while completely missing the partially occluded bystander visible through the foliage gap at the far left edge (2 to 3 m away).
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only the camera wearer's visible body parts in the immediate foreground (0.1 to 0.7 m away) against an unsegmented black background where the bush, loppers, and a distant, heavily occluded person at the far left edge (2 to 3 m away) are omitted. In frame 1, two overlapping masks labeled 'person' capture the wearer's left forearm on the left (about 0.3 to 0.4 m away) and torso and right arm on the right, positioned below the bush with both hands within arm's reach of the lopper handles. From frame 2 to frame 5, a single elongated mask extends from the bottom-right corner toward the upper-center (reaching 0.6 to 0.7 m forward) as the right arm stretches into the branches, shifting slightly rightward and rotating more vertically from frame 2 to frame 5 while the wearer's head and torso remain facing the bush and mostly out of the frame below. While the map cleanly delineates the silhouette of the reaching right arm from the visually complex foliage in RGB, it is highly unreliable in frame 3, where the right arm mask is misclassified with an overlapping 'carrot' and 'person' label, and across all frames it fails to segment the handheld loppers, the grasped branch occluding the wrist in frames 3 to 5, and the left hand holding the tool at the bottom edge in frames 2 to 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D hand skeletons in magenta on a black background, showing the camera wearer's hands in the immediate foreground while no full-body yellow skeletons or facing directions are detected for either the camera wearer (whose body is mostly out of view below the camera) or the partly occluded person at the far-left edge (2 to 3 m away). In frame 1, both the left and right hand skeletons are detected near the bottom-left and bottom-center at roughly 0.35 to 0.45 m from the camera and 0.15 m apart, with fingers curled inward around the lopper handles within immediate reach. In frame 2, only the right hand skeleton appears, elevated and shifted forward to about 0.65 m in the upper-left quadrant with fingers flexed around a branch, while the left hand at the bottom edge goes undetected. This map reveals the precise finger articulation and grip orientation of both hands in frame 1 and the elevated right hand in frame 2 more clearly than the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the pose estimation is unreliable whenever foliage partially occludes the skin, failing to detect the left hand in frames 2 to 5 and completely missing the reaching right hand in frames 3, 4, and 5 as its fingers curl behind the grasped branch and leaves.
